slides.text: Review the known phonemes with flashcards.
Listen to each prompt and write what you hear.
slides.teacher_note: Say each item clearly. Repeat once only if needed.
Model the sound clearly and flag Korean interference if needed.

slides.text: Introduce the lesson words orally before blending work begins.
slides.prompt: Point, say, and repeat each word.
slides.teacher_note: All lesson words are introduced here, including words with the new sound.

slides.text: Map each sound to print and blend the full word.
slides.prompt: Touch each sound, then blend the word.
slides.teacher_note: Model slowly first, then repeat at natural speed.

slides.text: Move from word reading into short controlled sentences.
slides.prompt: Point under each word and read the full sentence.

slides.text: Read the connected text smoothly and then reread for fluency.
slides.prompt: Read once carefully, then reread with smoother phrasing.
slides.teacher_note: Keep the text fully controlled and support fluent rereading.

slides.text: Use speech-to-print to encode the sounds you hear.
slides.prompt: Listen, segment, and write each item.
slides.teacher_note: Check sound-symbol mapping and full left-to-right encoding.

slides.text: Build early awareness that words can contain meaningful parts.
slides.prompt: Say the whole word, then notice the extra word part.
slides.teacher_note: Keep this light and oral for early groups.

slides.text: End the lesson at meaning, recall, and oral response.
close_questions: What sound did we learn today?
Which word did you read today?
Can you say one sentence from the lesson?
slides.prompt: Answer in a full spoken response where possible.
slides.teacher_note: Close with meaning, recall, and confidence.
